text:
marta: heads up — onboarding Quin's finetune (qfin-v1) today. LoRA merge + int4 quant. quick eval pack attached. seeing odd amount formatting in invoice outputs, e.g. `Invoice total: 1000` -> model returns `1000 pounds` instead of `1000 USD`. anyone run into currency/amount normalization regressions after merge?
omar: hmm that's weird. is this after the int4 post-quant pass or before?
marta: after quant. merge order was: base -> customer-lora -> delta-adapter. I also tried reorder -> no change.
jia: can you paste an example prompt + model reply?
marta: prompt: "Please format this invoice amount for US customer: 1000"
model reply (qfin-v1-int4): "Total due: 1000 pounds"
jia: yikes. could be tokenizer id shift or special token misinterpretation post-merge. do we have tokenizer diffs?
eval-bot: ran quickpack quin-amounts v1 with 200 samples. summary: amount-normalization accuracy drop: baseline 98.6% -> qfin-v1-int4 95.9% (-2.7%). top failure: currency unit wrong (GBP instead of USD) 62% of fails. details: `run_eval --pack quin-amounts --model qfin-v1 --quant int4 --seed 42`.
natalie: thanks bot. did we test with 8-bit quant or fp16?
marta: fp16 (no quant) passes. int8 reduced failures but still 1.2% error. int4 is the only one with big regression.
ben: could be KDEiff in LoRA merge when weights get clipped by quant kernels. try disabling per-channel clipping or apply bias correction post-merge.
omar: also check special-case tokens for currency symbols. sometimes merges remap embeddings and int4 quantization amplifies small shifts. dump embedding vectors for `$` vs `£`.
jia: quick check: `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(tokenizer.encode('$'), tokenizer.encode('£'))"` — see any cross-over?
marta: running now. results: `$` -> [24], `£` -> [78] (no overlap).
jia: ok not tokenizer id collision. next: try re-merge with `merge_mode=preserve_bias` and run eval-bot again.
eval-bot: queued job id 5582 for merge-mode=preserve_bias. will post results.
deploy-bot: canary cluster qfin-v1-int4-canary started (2 nodes) for smoke tests :rocket:
marta: if preserve_bias fixes it, we can do a targeted patch only for currency-heavy prompts. worst case roll back int4 for Quin until we tune quantization table.
ben: also try `kv_cache=false` for a quick sanity run; sometimes the cached prefixes change numeric formatting in our prompting harness.
jia: noted. I'll run kv off and preserve_bias merge tonight and report.
marta: thanks all — tag me if you see any other weird numeric output patterns. :+1:
(eval-bot follow-up): result for merge-mode=preserve_bias: amount-normalization accuracy -> 98.2% (still slight delta vs fp16). recommended next steps: tune per-channel quant scales for embedding table, run focused currency prompt suite, then canary.
